title: eval-harness: add prompt-set regression CI gates and quality-metrics integration
author: Jamal Carter
description:
Motivation: Prevent regressions in prompt-set quality by blocking merges that cause significant drops in eval metrics. This PR wires prompt-set based regression checks into CI, adds a metrics reporter, and provides an opt-out mechanism for experimental changes. Changes are intentionally incremental: CI gating evaluates a small set of critical prompt-sets and compares to stored baselines; failures surface a readable report and abort merge.

What this PR does (high-level):
- New GitHub Actions job (eval-gates) that runs lightweight evals against selected prompt-sets and uploads metrics as artifacts.
- A gating script (check_prompt_regression.py) that compares current metrics to baseline thresholds and exits non-zero when quality drops beyond configured tolerances.
- Baseline management tooling (scripts/generate_baseline.py & tools/ci/upload_baseline.py) to create and upload canonical baselines to CI artifact storage.
- Integrates the metrics reporter used by the eval harness so the job emits delta reports and a compact HTML summary for quick triage.
- Adds unit tests for gating logic and JSON schema validations.
- Documentation: docs/evals/ci-gating.md with runbook for maintaining baselines and adjusting thresholds.

Checklist:
- [x] Add GH Action job (eval-gates) and required secrets/permissions notes in docs
- [x] Implement gating comparator with configurable thresholds and tolerances
- [x] Add tests for comparator logic and CI artifact parsing
- [x] Wire metrics reporter and upload artifact step
- [x] Update docs and runbook
- [x] Add opt-out label (evals/skip-gate) support for experimental PRs

Operational notes:
- Default gating runs on push to feature branches and on PRs targeting main. It runs only on linux runners with a cached docker image for the eval harness to keep runtime under 12 minutes for the small prompt-set.
- Teams can opt out by adding label `evals/skip-gate` to the PR or by setting the `EVAL_CI_MODE=baseline-update` env to update baselines (requires maintainer approval).

Risks and mitigations:
- Flakiness: comparator tolerances default to conservative values and the job will not block for known noisy prompt-sets; those are listed in docs/evals/ci-gating.md.
- Performance: CI uses a tiny subset of prompt-sets (3 canonical prompts) to keep cost low; long-running full-suite gating is planned as a separate nightly job.

Related: Linear ENG-9482 (prompt regression infra), ENG-10421 (eval harness reporter), SUP-337 (customer-reported drift incident).

review_comments: Priya Anand: Can we make thresholds per-prompt rather than global? Some prompts are noisier and will need looser tolerances.
Jamal Carter (author): Good point — implemented per-prompt thresholds with a fallback global value. See check_prompt_regression.py:ThresholdProfile.
Marco Santos: Tests look good. CI failed initially due to missing artifact permission; recommend adding a note in infra readme about required repo-level permissions.
Jamal Carter (author): Added infra note and updated docs/evals/ci-gating.md with required permissions and token scopes.
Leah Kim: Is there a way to bypass the gate for large refactors where metrics are intentionally unstable?
Jamal Carter (author): Added `evals/skip-gate` label behavior and `EVAL_CI_MODE=baseline-update` env option (requires maintainer merge).
discussion_summary: Reviewers focused on flakiness controls and permissioning. Author added per-prompt thresholds, opt-out label, and infra docs after initial feedback. Marco confirmed CI permission change; minor fixes pushed and full CI green. PR approved by Priya and Marco, merged by squash.
